mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) over a 3-month period indicates reduced inflationary pressure, leading to a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower interest rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where CPI decreases by more than 0.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over a 3-month period signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increases by more than 5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5%, and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.3 percentage points in 3 months, it signals a tightening monetary policy with potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and UNRATE increases > 0.3pp in 3 months
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market stress
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is above 4.5% and UNRATE increases by more than 0.3pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over a 3-month period signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% over a 3-month period, it signals a strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over a 3-month period signals a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2% and GDP (GDPC1) increases by more than 2% over a 3-month period, it signals accommodative monetary policy with strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% and GDPC1 increases > 2% in 3 months
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with economic growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is below 2% and GDPC1 increases by more than 2% over 3 months.
